FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*') accepts the written form generically - the name needs no grammar token, which is why grep finds none in the Frontend; (2) IntrinsicCatalog.cs#Build carries Add(new("TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "i", "TestDayYyyyddd", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, false, 2002)) so MinArgs==MaxArgs==1 and IntrinsicBinder.cs (the 'given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs' guard) raises COBOL1504 on 0 or 2 arguments - the format's arity is enforced, not merely declared; (3) the result is IntrinsicType.Integer so a refModPart on the call is rejected by IntrinsicBinder's RefModFunctionResultClass arm ('is not an alphanumeric, boolean, or national function', ISO 8.4.3.3.3 SR2) - the grammar's optional refModPart* cannot over-accept here. (b) The grammar text was read directly rather than taken from the adjudicator: CobolExpressions.g4:332-336 is verbatim as quoted, and functionName (448-459) is IDENTIFIER plus nine reserved-word alternatives, so the hyphenated word lexes on the IDENTIFIER arm (longest-match beats any TEST prefix token). No whitespace defect. (d) THE REJECT HALF was verified arm by arm, not inferred: arity at IntrinsicBinder.cs:573-579 (COBOL1504, reached because TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD matches no bespoke arm between the 493 edition gate and the 565 generic path, and ArgKinds "i" does not end in 'l'); the ALL subscript at TryBindAllArgument (2553-2587) rejects with AllSubscriptNotRepeatable because sig.RepeatsAnArgument is MaxArgs == int.MaxValue and this row's MaxArgs is 1; the result ref-mod at FinishIntrinsic (132-149) -> ResultRefMod (169-195), whose category comes from IntrinsicSig.CategoryOf (93-99) mapping IntrinsicType.Integer to PicCategory.Numeric - not one of Alphanumeric/National/Boolean, so SR2 fires. IntrinsicSig's positional record header (IntrinsicCatalog.cs:52-57) was read to confirm the row's 1,1 really are MinArgs,MaxArgs. Both halves of the format are verified by reading, so rule 5's PARTIAL cost is not owed.
